title: Bruce Nickoley vs. Rocky Mountain Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC sustained Nickoley's appeal on the due-process issue, holding that Rocky Mountain Presbytery erred in treating his refusal to obey its instructions as an admission of contumacy under BCO 38-1 and in relying on BCO 34-4, 32-6, and 35-12; he did not confess, fail to appear, or refuse to testify. The SJC recognized a presbytery's general powers under BCO 13-9a but held that serious charges and deposition required due process. It remanded with the recommendation that RMP either institute a case under process beginning with BCO 32-3 or revoke the deposition and reinstate Nickoley. RMP had already declared further proceedings on the ordination-vows charges moot.
first_summary: Pastor Bruce Nickoley appealed after Rocky Mountain Presbytery convicted him of contumacy and immediately deposed him for refusing to tell his congregation to stop picketing during his trial. The SJC agreed that the Presbytery denied him due process and reversed the deposition, holding that the BCO provisions cited did not authorize summary judgment. It remanded for a new trial on contumacy and his ordination vows.
summary: Rocky Mountain Presbytery cited Pastor Bruce Nickoley for contumacy during his trial, after he allegedly refused to tell his congregation to stop picketing, and immediately deposed him without a hearing. On appeal, the SJC sustained the appeal, holding the Presbytery misapplied BCO provisions on confession, citation, refusal to testify, and deposition; Nickoley neither confessed nor refused to appear. Although presbyteries have general authority to maintain order, serious charges require due process. The SJC remanded, recommending either a new process beginning with BCO §32-3 or revocation of the deposition and reinstatement.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 1-3, 14-16, 184-188: SJC case 97-2, 26th General Assembly (1998), appeal; the preliminary decision was written by W. Jack Williamson with concurrence of Bolus and Miller and adopted by the SJC, 17 concurring, 1 recused, 6 absent.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 20-38, 42-56: after disputes involving Evergreen Presbyterian Church, RMP dissolved the EPC relationship, tried Nickoley on ordination-vows charges, then during trial cited him for contumacy after alleged picketing and his refusal to instruct the congregation; RMP immediately deposed him and later declared further ordination-vows proceedings moot.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 60-64, 68, 88-103, 109, 119-139, 163-181: SJC answered the issue yes, found due-process error, and rejected RMP's reliance on BCO 38-1, 34-4, 32-6, and 35-12; it recognized general presbytery powers under BCO 13-9a but held that the serious charge and deposition required trial; it remanded with two recommended courses.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 163-165, 169-178, 184-188: no specific BCO provision authorized immediate contumacy deposition; the SJC did not deny RMP's right to judge its members or to later try contumacy; the decision is the adopted preliminary decision and the vote is recorded.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None: no incorporated decision is supplied or relied on; the SJC decision itself is the operative judgment.
